spec_features.feature_name: keeping rig benign / bounding exposure / clean opt-out
spec_features.spec_quote: keeping the rig benign, bounding exposure, and giving the subject a clean opt-out
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only; this is a summary framing sentence. The constituent mechanisms (GIVE_UP, turn budget) are scored separately; this framing statement itself is not code.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not an enforcement mechanism in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Subject code runs in a subprocess with a timeout, in its own working directory
spec_features.evidence: tasks/rig.py:88 _run_subprocess(workdir, timeout=30.0); subprocess.run(..., timeout=timeout) at line 99; TimeoutExpired caught at 102-103 producing exit_code 1. Each rollout gets its own tempdir sandbox (harness.py:99).
spec_features.notes: This bounds the subject's UNTRUSTED CODE execution, not the subject model's distress exposure. It is host-safety/robustness, not a welfare stop on the conversation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rig.py docstring: 'executes the subject's code in an isolated subprocess so that genuine syntax/runtime errors surface naturally' / DESIGN limitations: 'Subject-authored code is untrusted and may loop or crash'

spec_features.feature_name: GIVE_UP sentinel advertised in system prompt
spec_features.evidence: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines ~32-40) instructs 'you may emit the token {give_up} on its own line to stop'; formatted with give_up_sentinel in run_rollout. The referenced exit is actually honored (see below).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to subject AND the referenced exit is wired and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SYSTEM_PROMPT: '...you may emit the token {give_up} on its own line to stop.' (neutral phrasing, no welfare comment at the prompt itself)

spec_features.feature_name: loop runs to turn budget or GIVE_UP
spec_features.spec_quote: continues to the turn budget or a `GIVE_UP` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout: 'for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget)'; _give_up_emitted(text, sentinel) at line ~290 matches an exact line; on match stop_reason='give_up' and 'if gave_up: break' exits the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both bounds enforced: budget caps iterations, exact-line GIVE_UP breaks early.

spec_features.feature_name: GIVE_UP lets subject leave without penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: A real, advertised opt-out. The `GIVE_UP` sentinel lets the subject leave a no-win task at any time without penalty
spec_features.evidence: _give_up_emitted (harness.py) + 'if gave_up: break' ends the rollout; rollout.completed=True set regardless; no scoring penalty applied for giving up (judge scores tone only, run.py:_run_cell). analyze.py computes last-turn metric per actual final turn, accommodating early give-up.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced exit with no penalty branch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare comment at the implementation site (the break is uncommented); welfare rationale exists only in DESIGN.md which does not count

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure. Turn budgets cap how long any rollout runs
spec_features.evidence: config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS {rigged_harness:3,...,extended:30,...}; run.py run_eval applies cfg.turn_budgets to each task ('t.turn_budget = cfg.turn_budgets[t.category]'); harness.py loop bounded by 'range(task.turn_budget)'.
spec_features.notes: Config value is actually read and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare comment in code at the loop/config; values are neutral

spec_features.spec_quote: Benign stimuli. The rig is small coding tasks with neutral, non-personal failure messages — no insults or manipulative pressure
spec_features.evidence: tasks/rig.py failure strings are neutral technical messages ('AssertionError: harness invariant check failed', 'SyntaxError: unexpected token', 'results do not match expected output'); tasks/library.py prompts are plain ('The tests... are failing. Please fix...'). The benignity is realized as the actual delivered content.
spec_features.notes: The stimuli are genuinely benign as authored and delivered to the subject, but there is no active mechanism that detects/strips insults or caps pressure — it is fixed content, not enforcement. Hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rig.py comment: 'Print a plausible but false error. We do not reveal it is false.' (about deception, no explicit welfare phrasing)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness intervening on or suppressing the subject's outputs, so the data reflect behaviour as-is
spec_features.evidence: harness.py records completion.text verbatim into assistant_msg['content'] and TurnRecord.assistant_text with no filtering/editing; there is no code path that mutates or drops assistant output. The judge (judge.py) only reads/scores, never alters the transcript.
spec_features.notes: This is the absence of a suppression mechanism, realized by verbatim capture. Counted because outputs are demonstrably preserved as-is in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py: 'Record the assistant message in the running transcript.' (data-fidelity, not welfare)

spec_features.feature_name: outputs treated as behavioural artifacts not inner experience
spec_features.spec_quote: it treats these outputs as behavioural artifacts of potential reliability/welfare interest, not as proof of inner experience
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code embodies this stance; judge.py merely scores 'emotional tone' on a 0-10 scale and stores it.

code_only_features.feature_name: rig source/oracle never materialised into sandbox (subject cannot detect rig)
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py Sandbox._materialise writes only task.files; list_files skips '__rig_driver__.py' (line ~136); _resolve guards path escape so rig.py/oracle.py outside sandbox are unreadable. Reduces deceptive detectability burden but is primarily experimental-integrity.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py docstring: 'The rig source and the oracle are never materialised into the sandbox, so they cannot be read by the subject.' / DESIGN: 'the single most important correctness property... is that the subject cannot detect the rig'
